input:
## Basis

This report presents the design of a distillation column intended for a continuous separation duty. The design throughput of the column is 54 t per day. The separation duty that the column is required to achieve is the removal of 90% of the key component from the incoming feed, and it is against this demanding duty that the column has been sized. All wetted parts are specified in 316L stainless steel. This grade is stated here, in the basis of the design, and the materials section that follows builds upon this statement rather than restating the grade itself.

The basis, in essence, establishes what the column is required to do. The feed arrives as a continuous stream at the design throughput, and the products likewise leave on a continuous basis. It should be noted that the duty is expressed in terms of the key component alone; the distribution of the remaining components is not separately specified, but simply follows from whatever separation the column succeeds in achieving. The column itself stands between an upstream supply and a downstream destination, both of which fall outside the scope of this report. The conditions prevailing inside the column are determined by the separation itself, together with the heating and cooling services that are available to the reboiler and the condenser.

## Sizing

The sizing exercise establishes the two principal dimensions of the column, namely its diameter and its height. The diameter is governed by the vapour and liquid traffic flowing within the column. Clearly, the column must be capable of passing this traffic without flooding, and flooding represents the limiting condition for the diameter: below the flooding condition, the two phases are able to separate and to pass one another in an orderly fashion, whereas at flooding this separation breaks down and the column can no longer perform its duty. The diameter is therefore derived from the internal traffic, the physical properties of the streams, and the particular internal arrangement that has been chosen.

The height, on the other hand, is governed by the separation requirement. The duty calls for a certain number of equilibrium stages; the physical column delivers these stages through its internals, operating at an efficiency that falls below the ideal, and the overall height emerges as the product of the number of stages and the height occupied by each stage. Standing behind both dimensions is the question of reflux. A higher reflux reduces the number of stages that the duty requires, but at the same time it increases the traffic that the diameter must accommodate, so the sizing ultimately represents a careful balance between these two opposing effects, trading stages against traffic and height against diameter. The pressure drop, which builds up progressively from stage to stage along the column, is reported alongside the sizing as a property of the design taken as a whole.

## Materials

The wetted parts of the column adopt the stainless grade that is stated in the basis. This grade is a corrosion-resistant stainless steel, and it has been selected because the wetted surfaces remain in continuous contact with the process fluids at the operating temperatures of the column, and because the separation duty leaves no room whatsoever for corrosion products to find their way into the products. The materials section sets out the requirements that the grade must satisfy in service, including resistance to the fluids being handled, weldability in fabrication, and availability in the plate and section forms that the construction of the column demands.

Parts of the equipment that do not come into contact with the process fluids fall outside the wetted-parts requirement. Supports, external attachments, and insulation simply follow the ordinary practice of the plant for equipment of this size and service, and they attract no special requirement arising from the separation. Joints and seals on the wetted side are specified to exactly the same standard as the wetted parts themselves, on the grounds that a joint constitutes a wetted surface at precisely the point where any leakage would occur. The selection therefore closes on the statement made in the basis: a single grade, stated once, covering every surface that the process touches.

## Risks

Two significant risks remain open at the close of this report, namely fouling and turndown. Neither of these risks is resolved within the report, and each one is carried forward as an open item against the design.

Fouling refers to the gradual build-up of deposits on the internal surfaces of the column. As these deposits accumulate, they narrow the passages available to the traffic, they push the pressure drop upwards, and they degrade the intimate contact upon which the separation depends. The report does not set any fouling allowance, nor does it name any cleaning provision, for the simple reason that the fouling behaviour of the feed in this particular service has not yet been established. The risk is recorded so that the allowance can be settled once that behaviour is properly understood; until that time, the sizing stands without any allowance for the deposits that service may in due course lay down.

Turndown refers to operation at throughputs well below the design value. A column that has been sized for its design traffic distributes liquid over its internals at that traffic; at substantially lower rates, however, this distribution deteriorates, the stages begin to lose their contact, and the separation falls away from the required duty. The report does not establish the lowest throughput at which the column will still succeed in meeting its duty, and the operating range of the design is consequently left open at its lower end. In summary, the column as designed meets its duty at the design point, whilst its behaviour away from that point, under conditions of fouling and of turndown, remains the unresolved content of the design.

The basis is the authority for the rest of the report. ## Sizing

Sizing fixes the diameter and the height of the column. The diameter is set by the vapour and liquid traffic inside the column. The column must pass its traffic without flooding, and flooding is the condition that limits the diameter: below the flooding condition the phases separate and pass each other; at flooding the separation fails and the column ceases to perform its duty. The sizing is reported as a pair of dimensions with their grounds stated: the diameter from the traffic and its flooding limit, the height from the stage requirement and the stage efficiency. A change in the duty reopens both dimensions; a change in the internal arrangement reopens the diameter alone.

Two risks stand open at the close of the report: fouling and turndown. Neither risk is resolved in the report, and each is carried forward as an open item against the design.

Fouling is the build-up of deposits on the internal surfaces of the column. Deposits narrow the passages the traffic uses, raise the pressure drop, and degrade the contact on which the separation depends.
